etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Middle English engendren, from Old French engendrer, from Latin ingenerāre.
senses: (obsolete, transitive) To beget (of a man); to bear or conceive (of a woman). [14th–19th c.]
(transitive) To give existence to, to produce (living creatures). [from 14th c.]

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (critical theory) To endow with gender; to create gender or enhance the importance of gender. [from 20th c.]
